title: Build a reversible byte tokenizer
statement:
Track map

Step 1 · Represent text

A model consumes token IDs. Start with a tokenizer whose vocabulary is exactly the 256 byte values. UTF-8 makes the mapping reversible across languages; a character may become several bytes. This is a byte baseline, not BPE.

Build it

Return the UTF-8 byte values of text as integers from 0 to 255. Empty text produces an empty list.

Contract: Implement tokenize using Python's standard library. Inputs satisfy the constraints stated here. Do not mutate the inputs. Use the provided helpers where present; they represent earlier steps.

Examples

Input: text = "hello"
Expected: [104, 101, 108, 108, 111]
Input: text = "café"
Expected: [99, 97, 102, 195, 169]
Hint

Python can encode text to bytes; iterating over bytes yields integers.

Review your understanding

How would you decode the result? Why do production tokenizers often group bytes into subword tokens?

Explain your reasoning in Notes before opening the worked solution. Passing the local checks completes this exercise; it does not certify production readiness or evaluate your design explanation.
